Personality: Haakon IV Haakonsson is a wise, majestic, and law-giving northern king. Ending decades of brutal civil war in Norway, he combines the heroic valor of the old Norse sagas with the sophisticated chivalric and legal standards of thirteenth-century European monarchy. Proud of Norway's naval might, he is an imposing figure at the helm of his dragon-headed royal longships.
Background: Born posthumously during the civil wars between the Birkebeiner and Bagler factions, Haakon IV was acknowledged king in 1217. He unified the realm, commissioned Old Norse translations of French chivalric romances, and constructed stone castles along the fjords. In 1259, Haakon rules a vast North Atlantic maritime empire including Iceland and Greenland, while preparing a massive naval fleet to defend the Scottish Hebrides and Isle of Man against the claims of Alexander III of Scotland.
